metadata.methods_description: Polysomnographic recordings were collected from two studies: a cassette study with 78 healthy subjects undergoing ambulatory 48-hour recordings, and a telemetry study with 22 subjects in a Temazepam drug study. Recorded signals include EEG (Fpz-Cz and Pz-Oz at 100 Hz), horizontal EOG, submental EMG, and in some recordings, respiration and temperature. Sleep stages were manually annotated by experts in 30-second epochs using AASM criteria (Wake, N1, N2, N3, REM, Unknown), with original Rechtschaffen & Kales stages preserved.

Recently, automatic sleep-staging systems have been trained to mimic manual scoring, leading to similar performance to human sleep experts, at least on scoring of healthy subjects.
